opposite_pole.label: End of a background/descriptive expository statement that states no outcome, typically closing on a trailing adjunct or prepositional tail ('over the site.', 'from that proximity.', 'illustrated in Figure 2.'); in code, ordinary non-return statement line breaks and indentation

rel_pos.label: H1 (from corpus top examples): the payoff token of a stated outcome: the word that completes the result/consequence of a conditional, causal or modal clause, or the returned value / final statement of a code branch

rel_h2.label: H2 (refined after the bank screen): the closing object/amount (or final period) of a hypothetical projection claim that a deliberate action or intervention WOULD/COULD change a measurable quantity -- money accumulated or saved, a bill or cost reduced, efficiency/yield/return raised, risk lowered -- typically with a possessor or a number on the target ('would have close to N3,000', 'would reduce your electricity bill', 'could increase their efficiency'). Weaker for will/may/present-tense action->result statements; near-silent for natural-event conditionals, abstract economic/physical laws, descriptive mentions of the same quantities, and code returns (the corpus code/long-context peaks did not reproduce in isolation, so H2 only claims the short-sentence prose behaviour).

rows.text: Paying an extra $100 toward the principal each month would shorten your mortgage by six years.
rows.why: would + financial action + measurable change to your mortgage term

rows.why: could + intervention + possessed yield increased by a stated fraction

rows.why: would + intervention + your risk lowered by a quantity

rows.why: counterfactual saving plan with would-have + money amount

rows.why: could + intervention + measurable performance quantity doubled (tests transfer beyond money)

rows.text: Cutting out sugary drinks could reduce a child's daily calorie intake by 300 calories.

rows.why: would + financial intervention + money saved with amount and beneficiary

rows.text: Our energy costs rose by about forty percent last winter.
rows.why: same quantity and amount but a past descriptive report, no hypothetical intervention

rows.text: The average commuter spends about $1,200 a year on gasoline.
rows.why: money amount and commuter vocabulary but a plain descriptive fact

rows.text: When the river rises, the low fields will flood.
rows.why: natural-event conditional with will, like the silent dam/ice bank items

rows.text: The efficiency of these solar panels was measured at 22 percent.
rows.why: efficiency + number but a measurement, nothing projected

rows.text: Would switching to LED bulbs really cut your energy costs?
rows.why: same projection content turned into a question; tests whether an asserted payoff is required

rows.text: Higher demand leads to higher prices.
rows.why: abstract economic law with no agent intervention, like the silent interest-rate item

rows.why: would-save embedded under whether; outcome not asserted

rows.why: mortgage/money topic but completed past fact, no projection
